summary: Resolve each order-card's ID from its data-csa-c-slot-id attribute (amzn1.yourorders.order-card.<ID>) when the card body carries no visible ID; never scrape generic hrefs for an order-ID shape.
reason: Amazon now ships order cards with a client-side-encrypted body (csd-encrypted-sensitive), so the order ID is absent from the card's visible text and ExtractOrderID(cardText) returns empty, dropping every order. The stable identifier moved to the card's data-csa-c-slot-id attribute. The 'Buy it again' recommendation links inside every card embed the session token (ue_sid), which is itself order-ID-shaped — scraping hrefs for an order-ID regex would assign every card that one token and collapse the whole page onto a single order, so only the slot attribute and unambiguous order-details/orderID= links are trusted.
validated_outcome: Against a real logged-in amazon.ca Your Orders page (10 encrypted cards) the parser recovers all 10 distinct order IDs; previously it returned 0. The --agent compact allowlist (compactListFields) keys off 'id', so orderId/placedDate/total/status are added there too — otherwise --agent order rows come back as {} with the ID stripped.
